entries.text: The date on the home page's "Key numbers" block is now machine-readable for search engines.

The tracker home page now has a dated "Key numbers" block near the press section: the same quotable figure, with its date and basis, that the tracker publishes for AI search tools, plus how to cite it.

The layoffs map no longer depends on an outside content network: its drawing library and map outlines are now served from this site at fixed versions. If the map still cannot load, you see the same figures as a table instead of an empty box.

On phones the tracker's first screen now shows the headline figure and a "Check my resume, free" button instead of a second theme switcher and the mascot drawing, and the cookie banner takes about a third of the screen instead of half, with Accept and Deny the same size side by side.

Accessibility fixes from an automated check: the region buttons now announce whether they are on, the jobless-claims list and two scrolling boxes are reachable by keyboard and read correctly by screen readers, the map has a proper label, and the source links on company, country and industry pages are large enough to tap (WCAG 2.2 target size).

Every country, state and industry page now has the free resume check line, worded for that place or sector ("Affected by a layoff in Germany?"). Company, country and industry pages now link to the same company, country or sector in our hiring tracker, where both trackers have a page for it.

The site menu's script loads again on company, country, state, industry and digest pages, where it used to fail with a console error. The date button that read "Last quarter" now reads "Last 90 days", which is the window it has always shown. The header's sign-up link on tracker pages now carries the tracker's own tag, and a brief database error while filtering quickly is retried instead of shown.

Clicking filters quickly no longer makes the tracker's data requests fail. Rapid clicks are now combined into one request with your final filters, a request that a newer click replaces is cancelled, and the server computes each uncached view only once at a time, with a short "busy, retry" reply (retried automatically) instead of an error when it is overloaded.

- /blog/ai-layoff-tracker/llms.txt is the tracker's own file (dk-forge/todo#1853): the map, a tracked link to the free resume check, and the year-to-date verified total with its "as of" date, its basis (effective date) and the press page that shows it. The figure is the press page's own, kept as the last good dated value when its hourly cache is cold. /blog/llms.txt is unchanged.

- Held rows: a row a guard cannot decide is stored as an unpublished (pending) post with a held_reason. It never reaches the table, totals, feeds, sitemaps or the seen-URL check. Keyed GET /held lists the queue; POST /held/{id} releases (publishes, after re-running the duplicate checks) or trashes (and suppresses the hash). - review-held.yml (daily, railway/review_held.py) puts each held row to the two referees; agreement releases or trashes, anything else stays held and turns the run red. - Negation guard (railway/negation_guard.py): any denial or negation cue in the count's own sentence holds the row ("not related to 60,000 job cuts", "denies cutting 500 jobs", "confirmed no layoffs"). It never drops or publishes on its own. Follow-up to row 183489 (Microsoft 60,000), trashed on 2026-11-18. - Tracker board footnote: when the headline (whole calendar year) and the YTD column (to today) differ, it states the gap, computed from the headline's verified total minus the board's own YTD cell, both by filing date.

- Referee rule 6 now names denials ("not related to 60,000 job cuts", "denies layoffs", "no layoffs planned") as not cuts. The extraction-time negation guard follows in its own PR. Row 183489 (Microsoft 60,000, 2026-11-13, a Syracuse.com outage headline) was trashed by two-referee adjudication (run 44414877612). - Monthly/quarterly report hero and press summary name their basis (effective date), which is why October reads 81,061 there and 88,265 on the filing-basis board. - Largest-entry cells without a record page link to a real period+company filter URL, never href="#". - Dataset dateModified is the last data write (alt_last_write), never the render clock; omitted when unknown. - Sign-up CTA: one utm_source=ai-layoff-tracker, utm_medium=referral; the "Affected by a layoff? Check my resume" block added to the ai-quotes hero and every report hero (utm_campaign ai_quotes / report_month / report_quarter / report_week / report_year).

- Conversion: every routed tracker page (methodology, sources, press, editions, reports, state-of-layoffs, publisher tools, US WARN registry, AI quotes, tracker health, country/state/industry pages) now gets the phone sign-up bar, and the standalone corrections and update logs carry the UTM-tagged "Check my resume" line (utm_campaign=public_log). The weekly finish line (run 44386250165) found no visible sign-up route at 390px on 11 pages and none at all on the two logs. Pinned in test_atr_signup_cta.py. - Finish line check: links with non-ASCII characters (country=Türkiye, Polish and Arabic employer names) are percent-encoded like a browser does, instead of being reported broken with status 0; a 429 from our own host pacing the crawler is retried with a back-off, and a lasting 429 is still reported. Both were false "broken link" results; the pages answer 200. Tests in test_finish_line.py. - Issue filer: finish_line_issue.py copied from asktherecruiter-sandbox PR #4352 (lists open issues instead of searching, tries the next token on a 422, pages through every issue and fails on an incomplete scan, logs GitHub's own error), with its tests.

- Email digest (owner ruling 2026-11-18): the weekly edition and its Ask The Recruiter blog section now go out Mondays at 06:00 New York time (was 07:37), and the weekly blog section lists every article published in that week instead of the newest three. A week with no articles carries no blog section. Pinned in railway/tests/test_digest_weekly_all_articles.py and test_digest_dst_slot.py.

- Company pages: two-question FAQ ("Did X have layoffs in YYYY?", "How many layoffs has X had?") with matching FAQPage JSON-LD. Every figure, date and source link comes from the rows the page lists; indexable pages only.

- Extraction (WEEKLY-23, AI-LAYOFF-TRACKER-5): when the primary model ends in upstream 429s or its rate-limit breaker is open, full extraction makes ONE metered call to a second model (`OPENROUTER_FALLBACK_MODEL`, default google/gemini-2.5-flash, the alternative measured 30/30 on the extraction gold set; empty turns it off) instead of dropping the candidate. Other errors never fall back. Tests in railway/tests/test_metered_call_rate_limit.py and test_extraction_model_choice.py. - Conversion: the main tracker page now carries the UTM-tagged "Check my resume" line under the hero (utm_campaign=tracker_home) and the phone sticky bar, so the flagship page has a tracked sign-up path on phone and desktop (CLAUDE.md conversion rule). Pinned in test_atr_signup_cta.py.

The daily AI layoff email now carries the same "open roles now" block as the talent email: current openings and the newest postings, each linking straight to the employer's own page. The monthly email no longer links to an archive page that is not published yet: it links the previous complete month, or no archive link at all.

Searching for an employer now finds it however its apostrophe was typed: "Children's Place" also finds entries filed as "Children’s Place". The news search also reads two more Dutch phrasings of job cuts.

Each entry now says which date it shows: Effective for a WARN notice (with the date it was filed, when the notice carries one), Announced for an announcement, and Layoff date for a filing or news report. None of these is a publication date. The methodology page explains each, and when first-listed dates began.

The monthly layoff digest now fits under Gmail's clipping limit, so the footer and unsubscribe link are always shown. The monthly "Who's hiring" section is now a short list of the five largest hiring plans with a link to the rest. The opening line no longer names a different employer from "Top employers"; the share of cuts resting on a single news report is stated at the top; "Multiple countries" shows one figure everywhere; and Russia is now placed in Europe.

In the layoff digest's region bars, a verified cut with no job location is now placed under the region of the employer's headquarters, on its own "by employer HQ" line, and a note says how many jobs were placed that way. The United States figure and the country list still count job location only.
The daily layoff digest now lists its ten largest cuts and links the rest, instead of up to forty rows. An amended Ohio WARN notice ("Update ...") is no longer listed as a second layoff.
The public copy of a sent digest email now shows any correction made to that edition, the same note the edition's archive page carries. The 2026 Week 45 copy now says its totals were revised.

The layoff digest no longer opens with, or names in its subject line, a figure that rests on one news report. The largest corroborated entry leads instead; single-report entries are still counted and listed, marked "Single report, not yet corroborated". Each edition now says in one line what its counts measure.
The inbox preview line of the digest emails now ends in one full stop. The talent daily had shown two.
The weekly layoff digest now labels its region bars "Verified job cuts by region". The bars count every verified cut, not only cuts attributed to AI.

The talent daily email reads more clearly. Every employer line now shows a country flag, or one neutral marker when no country is recorded. No region is called leading when signals with no recorded country outnumber it. Announced plans with no stated role count are grouped into one line. Every email now takes its postal address from one shared setting.

Each removal in the public corrections log now also records how many of its jobs counted toward the United States total. The site's own consistency check can then tell a deliberate removal of non-US rows apart from rows being re-counted into the US figure.

New layoffs published since 10 November now appear in the searchable table and the API again. A database column added in 2.20.306 never reached the live table, so new entries were published as pages but left out of search. The table now checks every column on each update and repairs one that is missing, and a failed save is logged instead of ignored. Entries with no real employer name, such as "Unknown", are now refused.

Each entry now shows when the tracker first listed it ("First listed 3 Nov 2026"), next to the date the source published. Entries listed before we started recording this show only the source date; we do not guess.
The sitemap that lists the corrections log and the update log now loads directly for search engines. It was being redirected to an address with a trailing slash.

The corrections log and an update log now have their own pages, at /ai-layoff-tracker/corrections/ and /ai-layoff-tracker/update-log/, so a correction or a change can be cited by URL. Every row from the /query API now carries created_at, the time the tracker first listed it, for rows read from the main table as well as entry pages. Rows listed before this release show it when their entry page records it and null otherwise.

The tracker's layoffs RSS feed is now advertised to feed readers in every page head and linked under "Cite this tracker". Company and state pages gain a share row (native share where the browser supports it, plus copy link, LinkedIn and X, with no third-party scripts). Five GA4 funnel events (digest signup, follow, embed copy, cite copy, resume prompt click) now fire through the existing Google tag with no personal data. Chart.js loads deferred, and a daily page-weight budget check watches the tracker and company pages.
The daily digest archive sitemap now loads for search engines. It was listed in the site's sitemap index but returned "not found", so Google could not discover the archived digest pages through it.
The blog home page and its paginated pages now really carry their own canonical URL. The 2.20.301 fix did not fire because the blog home is a static front page.

The blog index and its paginated pages (/blog/, /blog/page/2/ and so on) now declare themselves as their canonical URL, with any tracking query string removed. They previously pointed at /blog/blog/, a page that does not exist, which Search Console reported as "Duplicate without user-selected canonical".
Every country in the Talent Intelligence Tracker daily email now shows its flag, including ones like Bosnia and Herzegovina and Indonesia.

The Talent Intelligence Tracker daily email now opens with an at a glance box: how many hiring signals and employer-activity signals came in, the biggest announced hiring plan and the leading region. It explains the three kinds of signal in one line each, says up front that these are reported signals, and lists up to 10 hiring signals instead of 5.
Company filings that announce job cuts are now read from the right paragraph, so a long opening section can no longer hide the number of jobs cut.

Texas WARN notices are being collected again: notices filed since early October now reach the tracker. The Jeune Afrique feed was disconnected because the publisher now refuses our server; Francophone Africa is still covered through Financial Afrik and the local-language news sweeps.

News stories are being added to the tracker again. Since late October the news import had been skipping every story because a budget check misread the AI key as used up; the key had money left all along.

Behind the scenes: the owner is now emailed when the nightly update stops adding new layoff events from the news, for example when the AI service key runs out. From late October no new news events were added for several nights without anyone being told; that gap is now watched.

The Talent Intelligence Tracker daily email now names the region with the most signals (it could name a smaller one), links each employer to its open roles on its job board when we have verified that board, and says which dates its overall count covers and that the employer count is exact.

Layoff news now leads every edition. Blog reads sit in a labelled "Career resources" section, only for readers who ticked the articles box, and never make up a whole edition for a layoff-list reader. The career subject line leads with the reader benefit ("3 ways to strengthen your applications") and no longer carries article titles that name other products. Each read has a "Why it matters" line and a clear call to action ("Read the guide", "Read the comparison"), excerpts that are questions are replaced by the post's first real sentence, and the footer is shorter while keeping the unsubscribe link, the preferences link and the tracking disclosure.

The blog digest is now "Career Insights from AskTheRecruiter": one featured read with a short summary, then two more reads. The subject is the featured article's title. New subscribers get it weekly by default; existing subscribers keep their chosen frequency.

The Talent Intelligence Tracker daily email now leads with who is hiring. The subject names the top hiring development, announced hiring plans and open job-board listings are labelled and ranked separately, each employer gets one line, and the full data stays on the tracker. The email footer is shorter.
